title: Infinitary logic and countable model theory
abstract: Formalizes the syntax and semantics of infinitary logic and a broad collection of its classical theorems: Scott sentences and ranks, Karp's theorem, model existence, the sharp Morley--Hanf bound, Craig, Lyndon, and Malitz interpolation, López--Escobar definability, undefinability of well-ordering, the Silver--Burgess and Morley counting dichotomies, and an honest coded-fragment interface whose HF compactness theorem is derived from first-order compactness.

informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottSentence: Every countable structure in a countable relational language has an associated infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottSentence_charac: A countable structure satisfies the Scott sentence of another countable structure exactly when the two structures are isomorphic.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottRank: The Scott rank of a countable structure is the supremum of its element ranks plus one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottRank_lt_omega1: The Scott rank of every countable structure in a countable relational language is a countable ordinal.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.karp_theorem_w: Two relational structures admit a nonempty potential isomorphism exactly when they agree on every infinitary sentence over every branching carrier in their shared universe.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.model_existence: Every countable set of infinitary sentences in an equality-respecting consistency property over a countable language has a countable model.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.morley_hanf: Beth omega-one is a Hanf bound for every infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.Lomega1omegaHanfNumb: The Hanf number of countable-conjunction infinitary logic is exactly beth omega-one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_small_model_o: A sentence with arbitrarily large models has, at every infinite cardinality, a model realizing only countably many complete types.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_complete_sent: Every infinitary-small model belongs to a complete infinitary subclass contained in any prescribed sentence it satisfies.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_complete_kCat: A categorical sentence with arbitrarily large models has a complete categorical refinement at the same infinite cardinality.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.craig_interpolation: Every sentence entailment has an interpolant using only the function and relation symbols shared by its two endpoints.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.craig_pcSeparation: Disjoint projective infinitary classes can be separated by a single infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lyndon_interpolation: Every sentence entailment has an interpolant whose positive and negative relation occurrences lie in the corresponding shared occurrence sets.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.malitz_interpolation: An entailment with universal consequent in a relational language has a universal interpolant over the shared vocabulary.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_model_relPres: If a sentence has chains of every countable length, some model carries a relation-preserving map from the rationals.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrder_type_bound: The order types of all well-ordered models of one infinitary sentence are bounded below omega-one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrdering_undefin: No single infinitary sentence defines exactly the well-orders.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lopezEscobar_iff: A class of coded countable structures is Borel and isomorphism-invariant exactly when it is the model class of one infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lopezEscobar_action_: The López--Escobar characterization equivalently uses invariance under the natural permutation action on coded structures.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrderClass_not_m: The class of coded well-orders is not a Borel set in the logic space.
informal.gandy_harrington_for_relation: A Borel equivalence relation on a Polish space with uncountably many classes has a continuous Cantor injection of pairwise inequivalent points.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.silverBurgessDichoto: A standard-Borel quotient has at most countably many classes or exactly continuum many classes.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.morley_counting: Assuming the Silver--Burgess dichotomy, the number of isomorphism classes of coded countable models of an infinitary sentence is at most aleph-one or exactly the continuum.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.iso_borel_of_bounded: Isomorphism among models of an infinitary sentence is Borel whenever their Scott heights have a common countable bound.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.FamilyPresentation: A coded-family presentation packages codes with their indexed decoding and a certificate for admissible infinitary formation.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.CodedFamily: A coded family packages a certified family code with an explicitly indexed decoding, made unique by the presentation's decoding law.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.AdmissibleFragment: An admissible fragment is closed under exactly the coded infinitary families certified by its presentation.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.hfFragment: The hereditarily finite fragment consists of the infinitary formulas whose syntax contains no infinitary connective.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.hfAdmissibleFragment: The hereditarily finite fragment forms an admissible coded fragment without assuming compactness data.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.finitaryFragment_com: Every finitely satisfiable theory contained in the first-order image fragment has a model.
